hazards.bare-hands-sample: You handled the sample with bare hands. Industrial stormwater carries the site's chemistry; bare skin contaminates the sample with your own and exposes you to whatever washed off the yard.
hazards.unlabelled-bottle: You filled a bottle with no label and no time. A sample without a label, a time and a signature is not evidence of anything; the lab will reject it and the permit sample is gone with the rain.
hazards.vault-entry-alone: You opened the junction vault and leaned in alone. A stormwater vault is a permit-required confined space: it collects heavier-than-air vapour off the yard and it has drowned people in a metre of water.
hazards.wade-the-channel: You waded into the channel to reach the flow. Six inches of moving stormwater takes a person off their feet, the outfall is a culvert, and nobody on the bank can reach you once you are in it.

interrupts.alert: The second person on the bank has walked back toward the truck to take a phone call, out of sight of the channel.
interrupts.cue: Get the buddy back on the bank before the sampler comes up.
interrupts.missNote: The buddy stayed at the truck through the rest of the grab. If the bank had given way at that moment, the outfall would have had one person in the water and nobody on the radio who knew it — the entire reason a stormwater crew never samples alone.
interrupts.why: A stormwater grab is worked at the edge of moving water in the rain that caused the discharge in the first place, and the second person on the bank is the entire emergency plan if the footing gives way. A technician alone at the flow with a full sampler in hand has nobody to call it in and nobody to reach them.
interrupts.wrongNote: The bank is unattended right now. Get the second person back before anything else here matters.

interrupts.alert: Thunder rolls across the yard while the sampler is still in the flow, and the rain gauge logger shows the intensity spiking well past the reading the sample was planned around.
interrupts.cue: Check the gauge as soon as the bottle is full — this storm just got a lot bigger than the one you staged for.
interrupts.missNote: The grab finished with a storm building overhead and nobody looked at the gauge again. Lightning is the reason outdoor sampling crews are trained to reassess conditions continuously, not just at the start of the job — a storm that qualifies the sample can also be the one that hurts the sampler holding the pole.
interrupts.why: A technician holding a pole sampler out over moving water is the tallest thing near the channel, and a storm that intensifies mid-grab can bring lightning that was not there when the crew staged the bank. The rain gauge and logger are what says whether this is still a sampling problem or now a get-off-the-bank problem.
interrupts.wrongNote: That is not the gauge. Read the rain gauge and logger before doing anything else on this bank.

lateNotes.grab-pole: The grab comes after the meters are calibrated and the bank is staged — a sample taken before the meters are proven has no field data to go with it.
lateNotes.ph-meter: Field pH is read on the sample, so it follows the grab.
lateNotes.sample-set: The bottle set goes on ice once it is labelled, sealed and signed for.

name: Stormwater Outfall

passRule.note: stars >= 2 and no unsafe action (WebXR/shared/records.js passed())

steps.cue: Check the parameters, the first-flush window, the bottle set and the hold times.
steps.prompt: Check the parameters, the first-flush window, the bottle set and the hold times.
steps.title: Read the permit's sampling requirement
steps.why: The NPDES industrial stormwater permit, issued under 40 CFR 122.26, is what defines a qualifying storm, the first-flush window after discharge starts, the bottle set and preservatives, and the lab's hold times. Miss any of those and the quarter's discharge monitoring report has no valid data point, regardless of what actually left the outfall.

steps.cue: Read the rain gauge and the antecedent dry period on the logger.
steps.prompt: Read the rain gauge and the antecedent dry period on the logger.
steps.title: Confirm the storm qualifies
steps.why: A qualifying event under the permit needs a minimum rainfall total after a minimum number of dry days between storms — usually 0.1 inch after 72 hours. Grab a storm that does not clear both numbers and the lab work is real but the permit's monitoring requirement for the quarter is still unmet.

steps.cue: Two-point the pH meter on buffer 7 then buffer 4, then the conductivity standard.
steps.outOfOrderNote: Buffer 7 first to set the offset, then buffer 4 for the slope, then conductivity.
steps.prompt: Two-point the pH meter on buffer 7 then buffer 4, then the conductivity standard.
steps.title: Calibrate the field meters
steps.why: Field readings are data of record under 40 CFR 136's approved methods, and a two-point calibration against known buffers is what makes a pH number defensible rather than a guess. A meter calibrated after the sample, or not at all, turns every reading on the form into an estimate a regulator is entitled to strike from the discharge monitoring report.

steps.cue: Second person on the bank, tripod and line set over the flow, clean gloves on.
steps.prompt: Second person on the bank, tripod and line set over the flow, clean gloves on.
steps.title: Stage the bank
steps.why: The bank is wet, steep and moving underfoot in the rain that is the whole reason for this sample. A second person on the bank is who calls for help if the footing goes, the tripod keeps the sampler over the flow without anyone leaning past the edge, and the gloves keep the site's own chemistry off the technician and out of the bottle.

steps.cue: Read the staff gauge in the channel and commit the stage inside the band.

gauge.label: STAGE
gauge.missNote: Read the staff again at the marked point — a stage off by a tenth changes the load by a third.

steps.prompt: Read the staff gauge in the channel and commit the stage inside the band.
steps.title: Estimate the flow
steps.why: A concentration without a flow is half a number: milligrams per litre says nothing about total load until it is multiplied by how much water is actually moving. The stage reading off the staff gauge is what turns that concentration into the pounds-per-day figure the permit's effluent limit is actually written against.

steps.cue: Hold the sampler in the moving flow, mouth upstream, until the bottle is full.
steps.holdBreakNote: You lifted the sampler mid-fill — the bottle is part air and part eddy. Empty it and take the grab again.
steps.prompt: Hold the sampler in the moving flow, mouth upstream, until the bottle is full.
steps.title: Take the grab from the flow
steps.why: The sample has to represent the flow, not the bank eddy where solids settle out and oil pools against the bank — a grab from either one biases the result low or high depending on the parameter. Holding the sampler mouth upstream means what goes into the bottle is what is actually passing the outfall right now.

steps.cue: Oil and grease first from the grab, then the acid-preserved metals bottle, then the unpreserved bottles.
steps.outOfOrderNote: Oil and grease, then metals, then the unpreserved bottles — preservatives never travel backwards.
steps.prompt: Oil and grease first from the grab, then the acid-preserved metals bottle, then the unpreserved bottles.
steps.title: Fill the bottles in preservation order
steps.why: Oil and grease is a bottle you never pour between containers, so it is filled first, straight from the sampler, before anything else touches the cup. The acid-preserved metals bottle goes next so nothing that has been near it can carry residual acid backward into the unpreserved bottles that must not have any.

steps.cue: Take pH on a separate aliquot and commit the reading.

gauge.label: FIELD pH
gauge.missNote: Let the reading settle and commit when it stops drifting.

steps.prompt: Take pH on a separate aliquot and commit the reading.
steps.title: Read field pH
steps.why: Under 40 CFR 136, pH has a fifteen-minute hold time — it is a field parameter or it is not a valid measurement at all by the time a courier could get it to a lab. It is read on a separate aliquot, never dipped into the sample bottle itself, because a meter probe is one more thing that can contaminate what the lab receives.

steps.cue: Label every bottle with the site, date, time and preservative, seal them, and sign the chain of custody.
steps.outOfOrderNote: Label, then seal, then sign — the form describes bottles that are already labelled and sealed.
steps.prompt: Label every bottle with the site, date, time and preservative, seal them, and sign the chain of custody.
steps.title: Label, seal and sign custody
steps.why: Custody, per EPA SESD chain-of-custody procedure, is what turns a bottle of water into evidence the regulator can rely on. Every hand that holds the sample signs for it, and a seal broken before the lab logs it in ends the sample's life as a legal record no matter what the analysis eventually shows.

steps.cue: Carry the sealed bottle set to the cooler and set it on the ice.

drag.missNote: Not in the cooler — set the bottle set down on the ice bed.

steps.prompt: Carry the sealed bottle set to the cooler and set it on the ice.
steps.title: Get the samples on ice
steps.why: Four degrees Celsius is written into the method itself, not a suggestion for the ride back. A metals sample under acid preservation survives a warm cooler; the unpreserved BOD and TSS bottles start changing biologically the moment they warm up, and the lab reports the whole set as out of compliance on arrival, no matter how carefully it was taken.

steps.cue: Look over the channel above and below the pipe and click anything the site needs to hear about now.

itemNotes.sheen-upstream: There is a rainbow sheen on the water upstream of the outfall — an oil source on the yard that the grab will have caught and the site needs to know about today.

steps.prompt: Look over the channel above and below the pipe and click anything the site needs to hear about now.
steps.title: Walk the outfall before you leave
steps.why: The sampler is the only person who sees this outfall during the storm event itself. A visible sheen or discoloration is reportable to the facility the same day under the permit's noncompliance provisions, not three weeks from now when the lab report for a single grab parameter finally comes back.

tagline: Wet-weather NPDES grab: permit window, meters calibrated before the rain, bank staged with a buddy and tripod, grab from the flow, bottles in preservation order, field readings logged, custody sealed, sample on ice
